fig1_pe_vs_height.svg: $PE=mgz$ (potential_energy, $g=9.81$ m/s$^2$) for three masses. Each is a straight line whose slope is the weight $mg$, so lifting a 1000 kg mass 50 m stores 490 kJ. Compared with the internal energy of the same mass of working fluid this is tiny, which is why $\Delta$PE is dropped from most closed-system balances — but it is the entire operating principle of a pumped-storage power station.
fig2_datum_independence.svg: Potential energy has no absolute value — only differences are physical. Moving the datum shifts the entire $mgz$ line vertically, so the three choices disagree completely about how much potential energy a 200 kg body 'has'. They agree exactly about what matters: a 30 m fall changes it by -58.9 kJ (delta_PE) whatever the datum, and gravity does 58.9 kJ of work on the body (work_by_gravity $=-\Delta PE$). Pick any datum; just keep it fixed for the whole problem.
